newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Aznar defends free competition in digital TV.
newsitem.headline: Spain Aznar defends free competition in digital TV.

text.p: Spain's Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said on Monday the government will defend the cornerstones of free competition and freedom of choice in the country's digital television sector.
Aznar said the government's position on the sector was based on three fundamental principles: legality, competition and general interest.
"We are not going to shift from these principles and the government will defend these principles," Aznar said at a press conference.

When asked if Canalsatellite Digital would begin the distribution of its digital television project in the next few days, Aznar said the role of the government was to promote competition rather than deal with business questions.
"We will fulfil the law and hope others do too," he added.
Canalsatellite Digital is due to launch its digital satellite package on January 30.

It was given a big boost when media holding company Sogecable, Antenna 3 and pay-television firm Canal Plus were awarded the broadcast rights for Spain's first and second division soccer league games.
A Telefonica de Espana project had counted on Antenna 3 and its soccer audience to make it fly.
Telefonica announced on Friday it had signed a final agreement with domestic and international partners to create a digital platform in Spain.
